hook.title: The voting booth
hook.text: Your network doesn't directly produce probabilities. For a pixel with 256 possible brightness levels it produces 256 raw **enthusiasm scores** (logits). To turn scores into a fair vote share you exponentiate each (so all are positive) and divide by the total: **softmax**. For continuous data such as speech, there are infinitely many outcomes, so the network instead outputs the *recipe of a distribution*, the means and spreads of a few Gaussians to mix.
hook.recall: Remember the voting booth: scores → positive via exp → divide by total. For continuous data the net hands you the recipe (μ, σ) of a mixture, not a table.

explore.intro: Two tabs: softmax over four classes, and an RNADE-style mixture density.
tasks: Softmax: raise one logit. What happens to the others? Add 2 to *every* logit.
Mixture: move the three means apart. Is the output still a single hump?
explore.takeaway: softmax$(a)_i=e^{a_i}/\sum_je^{a_j}$ generalises the sigmoid. RNADE lets $\hat x_i$ define $(\mu_j,\sigma_j)_{j=1}^K$ of a mixture of Gaussians (use $\exp$ to keep $\sigma>0$).

build.prompt: Choose the output distribution for each data type.
build.template: Binary pixel → {0}.  A pixel with 256 intensity levels → {1}.  Real-valued speech sample → {2}.
build.explanation: Slides 11–13: binary → logistic/Bernoulli; $X_i\in\{1..K\}$ → categorical via softmax; $X_i\in\mathbb R$ → a continuous distribution such as a mixture of Gaussians.

questions.prompt: Which function turns a vector of logits into a categorical distribution?
questions.explanation: softmax: exponentiate then normalise. The voting booth.

questions.prompt: Logits $a=(0,\,0,\,\ln2)$. What is the softmax probability of the third class?
In RNADE why is $\exp(\cdot)$ applied to the network output that defines $\sigma$?
options: To make the output a probability
To ensure non-negativity of the standard deviations
questions.explanation: A standard deviation must be positive; $\exp$ of any real number is positive.

options: RNADE models each continuous $x_i$ with a mixture of $K$ Gaussians
For a continuous pixel, RNADE outputs a mixture of $K$ Bernoulli distributions
questions.explanation: Bernoulli is for binary data. RNADE’s components are Gaussians.

questions.prompt: A single pixel has 256 possible intensity values. How many logits does its softmax output layer need?
*“If I add 10 to every logit, the largest class becomes even more probable.”* Why is this wrong?
options: softmax is shift-invariant: $e^{a_i+10}/\sum_je^{a_j+10}=e^{a_i}/\sum_je^{a_j}$, so the probabilities don’t change
The largest class becomes less probable
The probabilities no longer sum to 1
questions.explanation: Only *differences* between enthusiasm scores matter in the voting booth, not their absolute level.
